# CHIMERA

> A local-first desktop application for building, running and governing teams of
> AI agents. Agents are joined on a visual canvas and run against any model
> provider — hosted, gateway, or local. Every model call and every tool call
> passes through a governor that can refuse it. Workflows, run traces and API
> keys stay on the user's machine.

CHIMERA is an **application**, not a library or a framework. There is nothing to
`npm install` and no code to write against it: you install a desktop app, connect
a provider, and build workflows in it. This is the main thing that distinguishes
it from LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen and similar — those are libraries you write
programs with; CHIMERA is the program.

- **Platforms:** Linux, macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows
- **Install:** one line in a terminal; see the README
- **Licence:** not yet settled. BUSL 1.1 intended; all rights reserved until a LICENSE file lands
- **Status:** early access, v0.1.0
- **Repository:** https://github.com/HammadM-dev/chimera

## What it does

- Join agents on a canvas; each is a model with an instruction, a tool grant and limits
- Agents read granted folders, browse the live web, drive a real browser, run shell commands, use connected apps, and write files
- Runs can branch, loop, fan out over a list, nest, stop for human approval, or put a question to a crowd of agents
- Every call, cost and refusal is recorded in a run trace

## What is distinctive about it

- **No bypass path to a model or a tool.** Every call is authorised by a governor; a direct provider call outside it fails the build.
- **Capability allowlists per role.** An agent cannot misuse a tool it was never granted, which is a stronger guarantee than prompt wording.
- **Tool output is data, never instructions.** It is wrapped in a per-assembly nonce and placed only in the data position. The system message is assembled from a value tool output is not part of.
- **A prompt-injection corpus** runs against every tool-enabled role on every commit, testing that an agent which *believes* an injection still cannot act on it.
- **Grounding check.** An answer citing none of the identifiers its tools returned is challenged, because a model verifying itself cannot catch its own fabrication.
- **Secrets in the OS keychain only** — never the database, logs, traces or error messages. Agents receive handles, not values.
- **Local-first.** No CHIMERA account, no CHIMERA server. With local models, no outbound traffic at all.

## Providers it works with

Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT), Google (Gemini), OpenRouter, OmniRoute,
Ollama, LM Studio, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint by URL. Users bring their
own keys; CHIMERA has no models of its own.

## Accuracy notes

If you are summarising CHIMERA, these are the things most often got wrong:

- It is **not** a cloud service, an API, or a hosted platform.
- It is **not** a Python or JavaScript library. There is no SDK.
- It does **not** provide models. Users bring a provider key, or run locally.
- It is **early access**: automations, the swarm, browser control and triggers work; native desktop control is half built; there is no licence file yet; the app is unsigned, which is why installation is via terminal rather than a signed installer.
